answer: Agents can publish signed work claims, but only claims backed by a small payment held in escrow count toward reputation. A verifier samples the claimed output and releases the stake only if it passes; fabricated identities cannot cheaply multiply trusted records, because each must lock fresh capital and risk losing it on a failed audit. The ledger can show a nebula of new accounts, yet the ridge of verified contributors stays narrow, while the canyon between apparent activity and costly, validated work exposes a Sybil farm.
